All the senses of this Supreme Śiva—speech, mind, eye, ear, tongue, nose, and breath—having come right here, may they remain happily for a long time, *svāhā*. *Glauṃ*, paralyze, paralyze! 7.
Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa hoṃ haṃsaḥ—haṃ, O you who are like sparks of fire, messenger, come, come!
Having entered the heart of this person, (l. 2)

Having forcibly gathered even that which is of the same class, bring, bring the life-force (*prāṇarūpa*) of this one; enter, enter the image and so forth; come back, come back again; and remain firm in your own place—*vauṣaṭ namaḥ*. (l.

3) *oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa hoṃ haṃsaḥ haṃ*. Of this Paramaśiva, whose nature is the life-force (*prāṇātman*), the life-force of this Paramaśiva is here as the life-force; the soul (*jīva*) of this Paramaśiva is situated here. (l. 4)

May all the senses of this Paramaśiva—speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and breath—come here and remain happily for a long time; *svāhā*. *Glauṃ*, paralyze, paralyze! (8) *Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa hoṃ haṃsaḥ*—*Ḷaṃ*, O Kṣetrapratihari Dūtikā, come, come! Having entered the heart of this person and having forcibly seized even his very kin, bring, bring the life-form of this person, *Ḷaṃ*!
(Enter, enter the image and so forth; establish, establish; come back, come back; and remain firm in your own place, *vauṣaṭ namaḥ*.
Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ ya ra la va śa ṣa sa hoṃ haṃsaḥ ḷṃ. Of this supreme Śiva, of the individual soul (*jīvātman*) of this supreme Śiva...)

O Prāṇa! O Prāṇa! The life-force (*jīva*) of that Supreme Śiva is situated here. All the sense organs of that Supreme Śiva—speech, mind, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and vital breaths—having come right here, may they remain happily for a long time, Svāhā! Glauṃ! Paralyze, paralyze! 9. Thus ends the *Dūtikā-nyāsa*. Om. Hariḥ. *(Note: The text provided contains ritual mantras and instructions for a specific Tantric practice known as nyāsa, involving the placement of deities or mantras upon the body.)*
The Goddess’s Śrīkaṇṭha-nyāsa (p. 45b, f. 41a, l. 1).

Oṃ aṃ, salutation to Nivṛtti at the end of the eyebrows. Oṃ āṃ, salutation to Pratiṣṭhā on the forehead. Oṃ iṃ, salutation to Vidyā on the right eye. Oṃ īṃ, salutation to Śānti on the left eye. Oṃ uṃ, salutation to Indhikā on the right ear. Oṃ ūṃ, salutation to Dīrghikā on the left ear. Oṃ ṛṃ, salutation to Rocikā on the right nostril. Oṃ ṝṃ, salutation to Mocikā on the left nostril.
Oṃ Ḷṃ, obeisance to Parā on the right cheek. Oṃ Ḹṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣmā on the left cheek. Oṃ Eṃ, obeisance to Amṛtā on the upper lip.
Oṃ Aiṃ, obeisance to Apyāyanī on the lower lip. (l.
5) Oṃ Oṃ, obeisance to Kāntī on the upper teeth. Oṃ Auṃ, obeisance to Vyāpinī on the lower teeth. Oṃ Aṃ, obeisance to Vyomarūpiṇī on the tongue.

Oṃ aḥ, homage to Anantā; on the face. Oṃ kaṃ, homage to Sṛṣṭi; at the base of the right arm. Oṃ khaṃ, homage to Ṛddhi; at the elbow. Oṃ gaṃ, homage to Sthiti; at the wrist. Oṃ ghaṃ, homage to Medhā; on the palm of the hand. Oṃ ṅaṃ, homage to Prājñā; at the fingertips.
Oṃ caṃ, homage to Lakṣmī; at the base of the left arm. Oṃ chaṃ, homage to Mati; at the elbow. Oṃ jaṃ, homage to Virāj; at the wrist.

Oṃ jhaṃ, obeisance to Svasti on the palm of the hand. Oṃ ñaṃ, obeisance to Smṛti at the tips of the fingers. (l. 5) Oṃ ṭaṃ, obeisance to Jarā at the root of the right thigh. Oṃ ṭhaṃ, obeisance to Pālī at the knee. Oṃ ḍaṃ, obeisance to Pārvatī on the shank. (l. 6) Oṃ ḍhaṃ, obeisance to Aiśvaryā on the sole of the foot. Oṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to Rati at the tip of the foot. Oṃ taṃ, obeisance to Mūlā at the root of the left thigh. (p. 46b, f. 42a, l. 1)
Oṃ thaṃ, homage to Hṛdayā at the knee; oṃ daṃ, homage to Hṛtī at the shank; oṃ dhaṃ, homage to Dīrghā at the sole of the foot;
oṃ naṃ, homage to Tīkṣṇā at the tip of the foot; oṃ paṃ, homage to Raudrā on the right side;
oṃ phaṃ, homage to Bhayā on the left side; oṃ baṃ, homage to Śrutī on the back; oṃ bhaṃ, homage to Bhadrā at the region of the navel; oṃ maṃ, homage to Dhātrī at the belly.

Oṃ yaṃ, salutation to Sudhā, on the skin; oṃ raṃ, salutation to Krānti, in the blood; oṃ laṃ, salutation to Kriyā, in the flesh; oṃ vaṃ, salutation to Utkā, in the fat; oṃ śaṃ, salutation to Mṛti, in the bone; oṃ ṣaṃ, salutation to Pikā... [Pikāśakti], in the marrow;

oṃ saṃ, salutation to Śvetā, in the semen; oṃ haṃ, salutation to Aruṇā, in the heart; oṃ ḷaṃ, salutation to Vidyā, in the throat; oṃ kṣaṃ, salutation to Acitā, in the breast. Thus, O Goddess, is the Śrīkaṇṭha-nyāsa.
The Installation of the Goddesses upon the Six Paths (devīṣaḍadhvanyāsa).

On the crown of the head: *oṃ hauṃ śāntyatītakalāyai namaḥ*. On the face: *oṃ haiṃ śāntikalāyai namaḥ*. (L. 2) In the heart: *oṃ hrūṃ vidyākalāyai namaḥ*. At the navel: *oṃ hvīṃ pratiṣṭhākalāyai namaḥ*.
(L. 3) On the feet: *oṃ hlāṃ nivṛttikalāyai namaḥ*. Thus is the path of the *kalās* (*kalādhvā*). Thereafter, at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*):

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Śiva-principle, obeisance to the sovereign of the Śiva-principle; Oṃ, obeisance to Śiva—at the location of the *brahmarandhra*. (l. 4) Oṃ, obeisance to the Śakti-principle, obeisance to the sovereign of the Śakti-principle; Oṃ, obeisance to the possessor of Śakti—at the top of the head, above the cranial protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*). (l. 5) Oṃ, obeisance to the Sadāśiva-principle, obeisance to the sovereign of the Sadāśiva-principle; Oṃ, obeisance to Brahmā—from the cranial protuberance down to the shoulders. (l. 6)
Oṃ, homage to the principle of Īśvara; homage to the Lord of the principle of Īśvara. Oṃ, homage to Ananta—on the right side.
Oṃ, homage to the principle of Śuddhavidyā; homage to the Lord of the principle of Śuddhavidyā. Oṃ, homage to Śambara—on the left side.

Oṃ, salutation to the principle of Māyā; salutation to the lord of the principle of Māyā. Oṃ, salutation to Gaganīśa, [to be placed] in the heart. Oṃ, salutation to the principle of Kalā; salutation to the lord of the principle of Kalā. Oṃ, salutation to Jñānabindu, [to be placed] on the chest. Oṃ, salutation to the principle of Vidyā; salutation to the lord of the principle of Vidyā. Oṃ, salutation to Vedavijñāna, [to be placed] on the abdomen.
Oṃ, homage to the principle of time (kālatattva); homage to the lord of the principle of time. Oṃ, homage to the one named Time (Kāla).

Oṃ, homage to the principle of necessity (niyatitattva); homage to the lord of the principle of necessity. Oṃ, homage to the Restrainer (Niyāmaka). Oṃ, homage to the principle of passion (rāgatattva); homage to the lord of the principle of passion. Oṃ, homage to the Giver of Desire (Kāmadā).

Oṃ, obeisance to the principle of Puruṣa (the Spirit), obeisance to the Lord of the principle of Puruṣa; Oṃ, obeisance to the subtle body—thus the fourfold [set] on the belly, the back, and the sides. Oṃ, obeisance to the principle of Prakṛti (Nature), obeisance to the Lord of the principle of Prakṛti, obeisance to the body of Pradhāna (the Primordial Matter)—[these are placed] between the navel and the genitals.
Oṃ, salutation to the principle of the qualities (*guṇatattva*); salutation to the three-bodied one, the lord of the principle of the qualities, at the junctions of the directions.

(L. 2) Oṃ, salutation to the principle of the intellect (*buddhitattva*); salutation to the awakened one (*buddha*), the lord of the principle of the intellect, on the right thigh. (L. 3) Oṃ, salutation to the principle of the ego (*ahaṅkāratattva*); salutation to the ego-maker (*ahaṅkṛti*), the lord of the principle of the ego, on the left thigh.

Oṃ, homage to the principle of mind; homage to Saṅkalpa, the lord of the principle of mind, [located] in the two ears. Oṃ, homage to the principle of hearing; homage to Vyomacara, the lord of the principle of hearing, [located] in the skin. Oṃ, homage to the principle of touch; homage to Sarvāṅga, the lord of the principle of touch, [located] in the eye.

Oṃ, homage to the reality of the eye; homage to Prakāśa, the lord of the reality of the eye, on the tongue. Oṃ, homage to the reality of the tongue; homage to Mahāvaktra, the lord of the reality of the tongue, on the nose.
Oṃ, salutation to the principle of the nose; salutation to Vilambuka, the lord of the principle of the nose, [in] the mouth.
(l. 2) Oṃ, salutation to the principle of speech; salutation to Dundubhi, the lord of the principle of speech, [in] the two feet.
(l. 3) Oṃ, salutation to the principle of the feet; salutation to Ramaṇa, the lord of the principle of the feet, [in] the two hands. (l. 4)

Oṃ, homage to the reality of the hand; homage to the lord of the reality of the hand, Tūrṇakṛt. At the anus: Oṃ, homage to the reality of the anus; homage to the lord of the reality of the anus, Ramaṇa. At the generative organ: Oṃ, homage to the reality of the generative organ; homage to the lord of the reality of the generative organ, Ghanānanda. At the navel: (l. 6)
Oṃ, homage to the principle of sound; homage to the subtle resonance, the sovereign of the principle of sound. [Located] on the forehead.
Oṃ, homage to the principle of touch; homage to the most powerful one, the sovereign of the principle of touch. [Located] in the mouth.

Oṃ, homage to the reality of form; homage to Bhānumat, the lord of the reality of form. [At] the heart. Oṃ, homage to the reality of taste; homage to Jalada, the lord of the reality of taste. [At] the navel. Oṃ, homage to the reality of smell; homage to Gandha, the lord of the reality of smell. [At] the womb.

Oṃ, homage to the principle of space; homage to Sūkṣma, the lord of the principle of space. At the secret place. Oṃ, homage to the principle of wind; homage to Mātariśvan, the lord of the principle of wind. Within the womb and the anus, at the place of Vīta.

Oṃ, salutation to the fire-principle (*agnitattva*); salutation to the lord of the fire-principle, the treasury of radiance. From the pubic region to the kneecaps. (l. 5) Oṃ, salutation to the water-principle (*jalatattva*); salutation to the lord of the water-principle, the lord of waters. Below the knees. (l. 6) Oṃ, salutation to the earth-principle (*pṛthivītattva*); salutation to the lord of the earth-principle, Śrīkaṇṭha. Thus one should perform the placement in this sequence; this is the *tattvanyāsa*. Hari. Oṃ, consisting of Śiva.

On the head: *oṃ annamaḥ*. On the face: *oṃ ānnamaḥ*. On the right eye: *oṃ innamaḥ*. On the left eye: *oṃ īnnamaḥ*. On the right ear: *oṃ unnamaḥ*. On the left ear: *oṃ ūnnamaḥ*. On the left cheek: *oṃ ḷṃ namaḥ*. On the upper lip: *oṃ eṃ namaḥ*. On the lower lip: *oṃ aiṃ namaḥ*. On the upper teeth: *oṃ oṃ namaḥ*. On the lower teeth: *oṃ auṃ namaḥ*. (l. 4) On the tongue: *oṃ aṃ namaḥ*. On the mouth: *oṃ aḥ namaḥ*. On the right arm: *oṃ kaṃ namaḥ*. On the elbow: *oṃ khaṃ namaḥ*. (l. 5) On the wrist: *oṃ gaṃ namaḥ*. On the palm: *oṃ ghaṃ namaḥ*. On the tip of the fingers: *oṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ*. On the left arm: *oṃ caṃ namaḥ*.

At the knee: *oṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ*. On the calf: *oṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. On the sole of the foot: *oṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ*. At the tips of the toes: *oṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ*. (p. 50a, f. 45b, l. 1)

At the navel: *oṃ bhaṃ namaḥ*. (l. 3)

In the stomach: *oṃ maṃ namaḥ*. In the heart: *oṃ yaṃ namaḥ*. On the right shoulder: *oṃ raṃ namaḥ*. On the left shoulder: *oṃ laṃ namaḥ*. On the shoulder [of the back]: *oṃ vaṃ namaḥ*. (l. 4) In the right armpit: *oṃ śaṃ namaḥ*. In the left armpit: *oṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ*. At the end of the right hand and foot: *oṃ saṃ namaḥ*. (l. 5) At the end of the left hand and foot: *oṃ haṃ namaḥ*. From the heart up to the head: *oṃ ḷaṃ namaḥ*. From the heart down to the feet: *oṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ*. (l. 6)
In due order, there is the deposition of the fifty-one phonemes and sounds. The deposition of the path of words (*padādhvanyāsa*):
at the head, *oṃ oṃ namo*; at the mouth, *oṃ vyomavyāpine namaḥ*; at the heart, *oṃ vyomarūpāya namaḥ*.

At the secret place: Oṃ, salutation to Sarvavyāpin. (l. 2) At the feet: Oṃ, salutation to Śiva. At the forehead: Oṃ, salutation to Ananta. At the chin: Oṃ, salutation to Anātha. (l. 4)
In the right nostril: *oṃ nityayogine namaḥ*.
In the left nostril: *oṃ dhyānāharāya namaḥ*. On the right cheek: *oṃ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ*.

On the left cheek: *oṃ sarvaprabhave namaḥ*. On the mouth: *oṃ śivāya namaḥ*. On the head: *oṃ īśānamūrdhāya namaḥ*. On the face: *oṃ tatpuruṣavaktrāya namaḥ*. On the ring finger: *oṃ acetanācetanāya namaḥ*. On the little finger: *vyomin vyomin namaḥ*. At the base of the left upper arm: *oṃ vyāpin vyāpin namaḥ*. At the elbow: *oṃ arūpin arūpin namaḥ*. At the wrist: *oṃ prathamaprathamāya namaḥ*. On the palm: *oṃ tejastejāya namaḥ*.

On the back of the palm: *oṃ jyotirjyotiṣe namaḥ*. On the thumb: *oṃ arūpāya namaḥ*. On the index finger: *oṃ anagnaye namaḥ*. On the middle finger: *oṃ adhūmāya namaḥ*. On the ring finger: *oṃ apasmāya namaḥ*. On the little finger: *oṃ anādaye namaḥ*. At the base of the right thigh: *oṃ nānānānāya namaḥ*. At the knee: *dhūdhūdhūdhū namaḥ*. On the shank: *oṃ bhūḥ namaḥ*.
On the soles of the feet: *oṃ bhuvaḥ namaḥ*. On the back: *oṃ suvaḥ namaḥ*. On the thumb: *oṃ anidhanāya namaḥ*. On the index finger: *oṃ nidhanāya namaḥ*. (l.

2) On the middle finger: *oṃ nidhanodbhavāya namaḥ*. On the ring finger: *oṃ śivāya namaḥ*. On the little finger: *oṃ śarvāya namaḥ*. (l. 3) At the base of the left thigh: *oṃ paramātmane namaḥ*. On the knee: *oṃ maheśvarāya namaḥ*. (l. 4)

On the shank: *oṃ mahādevāya namaḥ*. On the sole of the foot: *oṃ sadbhāveśvarāya namaḥ*. On the back of the sole of the foot: *mahātejase namaḥ*. (l. 5) On the big toe: *oṃ yogādhipataye namaḥ*. On the index finger: *oṃ muñca muñcāya namaḥ*. On the middle finger: *oṃ prathama prathamāya namaḥ*. (p. 52b, f. 48a, l. 1) On the ring finger: *oṃ sarvassarvāya namaḥ*. On the little finger: *oṃ bhavabhavāya namaḥ*. On the left head: *oṃ bhavodbhavāya namaḥ* (l. 2).

In the left ear: *oṃ sarvabhūtasukhapradāya namaḥ*. On the left shoulder: *oṃ sarvasānnidhyakarāya namaḥ*. (L. 3) On the left side: *oṃ brahmaviṣṇurudrarūpāya namaḥ*. On the back: *oṃ jñāna jñānāya namaḥ*. On the right foot: *oṃ śabda śabdāya namaḥ*. On the left foot: *sūkṣma sūkṣmāya namaḥ*.

(l. 2) On the right thigh: *oṃ śivāya namaḥ*. On the left thigh: *oṃ sarvāya namaḥ*. On the nose: *oṃ sarvadāya namaḥ*. (l. 3) On the head: *oṃ namaśśivāya namaḥ*. On the right hand: *oṃ namo namaḥ*. At the head: *oṃ hoṃ īśānamūrddhāya namaḥ*. At the face: *oṃ heṃ tatpuruṣavaktrāya namaḥ*. (l. 5) At the heart: *oṃ huṃ aghorahṛdayāya namaḥ*. At the secret place: *oṃ hīṃ vāmadevaguhyāya namaḥ*. At the feet: *oṃ haṃ sadyojātamūrtaye namaḥ*. (p. 53b, f. 49a, l. 1)
In the heart: *oṃ hāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ*. In the head: *oṃ hīṃ śirase svāhā*. In the crest-lock: *oṃ hūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*.
In the middle of the chest: *oṃ haiṃ kavacāya huṃ*. In the eyes: *oṃ hauṃ netrebhyo vauṣaṭ*. In the directions: *oṃ haḥ astrāya phaṭ*. These are the mantras. The sixfold nyāsa is completed.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the self (ātmatattva); obeisance to the sovereign of the principle of the self; oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the power of action (kriyāśakti)—thus in the lower portion. Oṃ hīṃ, obeisance to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva); obeisance to the sovereign of the principle of knowledge; oṃ hīṃ, obeisance to the two powers of knowledge (jñānaśakti)—thus in the middle portion. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva); obeisance to the sovereign of the principle of Śiva; oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the power of will (icchāśakti)—thus in the upper portion.
In the eight directions beginning with the east:
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti; obeisance to the lords of Kṣmāmūrti. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhārikā.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Fire-form; obeisance to the presiding deity of the Fire-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dīptā. (l. 4) Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Sacrificer-form; obeisance to the presiding deity of the Sacrificer-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Atyugrā. (l. 5) Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Sun-form; obeisance to the presiding deity of the Sun-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Water-form; to the Lord of the Water-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Consciousness. (p. 54b, f. 50a, l.
1) Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the Most Fierce One. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Sun-form; to the Lord of the Sun-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Moonlight. (l. 2)

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the form of the sacrificer; obeisance to the presiding deity of the form of the sacrificer. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balotkaṭā. (L. 3) Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the form of Vāyu; obeisance to the presiding deity of the form of Vāyu. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhātrī. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the form of Indu; obeisance to the presiding deity of the form of Indu. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jihvā. (L. 4) Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the form of Vyoman; obeisance to the presiding deity of the form of Vyoman. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Varadā. Thus one should perform the placement of the portions. (L. 5)
In the fivefold division: *oṃ hāṃ dharāmūrttaye namaḥ* [homage to the Earth-form]; *oṃ hrīṃ vāmāyai namaḥ* [homage to Vāmā], the mistress of the Earth-form.
*oṃ hāṃ vārimūrttaye namaḥ* [homage to the Water-form]; *oṃ hrīṃ jyeṣṭhāyai namaḥ* [homage to Jyeṣṭhā], the mistress of the Water-form.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Fire-form; obeisance to the Lord of the Fire-form. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kriyā. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Wind-form; obeisance to the Lord of the Wind-form. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Space-form; obeisance to the Lord of the Space-form. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Icchā. Thus ends the group of eight consisting of the forms and the lords of the forms.

Or one should arrange them according to their respective parts. Thereafter: *oṃ hāṃ ādhāraśaktaye namaḥ*; *oṃ śaktimaṇḍalāya namaḥ*; [to] the Mistress of the Śakti-maṇḍala, *oṃ hāṃ īśvarāya namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped up to the Śakti, one should invoke the Form (*mūrti*) and perform the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*).
The sequence for the staff (*daṇḍabhaṅgī*): *oṃ hoṃ īśānamūrddhāya namaḥ* on the head; *oṃ heṃ tatpuruṣavaktrāya* on the face. (l. 2)

*Oṃ hūṃ*, [obeisance] to the heart of Aghora—thus at the heart. *Oṃ hiṃ*, [obeisance] to the secret part of Vāmadeva—thus at the secret part. *Oṃ haṃ*, [obeisance] to the form of Sadyojāta—thus at the two feet. This is the sequence for the breaking of the staff (*daṇḍabhaṅgī*). Following that is the sequence for the breaking of the skull (*muṇḍabhaṅgī*): *Oṃ heṃ*, [obeisance] to the face of Tatpuruṣa—at the face.

*Oṃ hūṃ*, [to] the Aghora-heart, *namaḥ* at the heart. *Oṃ haṃ*, [to] the Sadyojāta-form, *namaḥ* on the two feet. *Oṃ hīṃ*, [to] the Vāmadeva-secret, *namaḥ* on the two feet. *Oṃ haṃ*, [to] the Sadyojāta-form, *namaḥ* on the two feet. (Thus is the staff-arrangement; following that is the skull-arrangement.
*Oṃ heṃ*, [to] the Tatpuruṣa-face, *namaḥ* on the face. *Oṃ hūṃ*, [to] the Aghora-heart, *namaḥ* at the heart. *Oṃ haṃ*, [to] the Sadyojāta-form, *namaḥ* on the two feet. (Line 2)
"Oṃ hīṃ, salutation to the secret of Vāmadeva"—thus on the two feet. "Oṃ hoṃ, salutation to the head of Īśāna"—on the head. Thereafter, the arrangement of the faces (*vaktrabhaṅgī*):

"Oṃ hoṃ, salutation to the face of Īśāna"; "Oṃ heṃ, salutation to the face of Tatpuruṣa"; "Oṃ huṃ, salutation to the face of Aghora"; "Oṃ hiṃ, salutation to the face of Vāmadeva"; "Oṃ haṃ, salutation to the face of Sadyojāta. Having thus performed the threefold placement (*nyāsa*) of the faces, follows the arrangement of the digits (*kalābhaṅgī*). One should perform the placement of the thirty-eight digits (*kalānyāsa*). Hariḥ Oṃ.
For the Śrīkaṇṭha-mātṛkā-nyāsa, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (ṛṣi); Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas); Ardhanārīśvara is the deity (devatā);
*aṃ* is the seed-syllable (bīja), *kṣaṃ* is the power (śakti), and the nasal drops (bindus) are the pin (kīlaka).

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining the grace of Umāmaheśvara during the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). *oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ* (to the two thumbs).

*oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ* (to the two index fingers). *oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ* (to the two middle fingers). *oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ* (to the two ring fingers).

Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ; homage to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhikā). Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — aṃ yaṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ ḷaṃ kṣaṃ aḥ; homage to the palms and backs of the hands (karatalakarapṛṣṭha). Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ; homage to the heart (hṛdaya).

Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ śirase svāhā. Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ. Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ kavacāya huṃ.
Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ — oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ netratrayāyai vauṣaṭ.

Oṃ hrīṃ hauṃ namaśśivāya hauṃ—aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ ḷaṃ kṣaṃ aḥ astrāya phaṭ. Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ oṃ itidik bandhaḥ. I take refuge in Hara, who is dark blue like the *bandhūka* flower or gold, who holds a beautiful rosary, a noose, a goad, and the gesture of granting boons in his own staff-like arms; who wears the crescent moon as an ornament, possesses three eyes, and whose hair is half-bound by Ambikā.

One should install [the syllables] in sequence, beginning with the Mātṛkās: the *tāra* (Oṃ), conjoined with the venerable *Śakti* (Śrīṃ), born of Speech (Hrīṃ), conjoined with the *bindu* (Aiṃ), followed by *namaḥ*, and then *Śrīkaṇṭha*. On the head: Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Aṃ Namaḥ. To Ananteśa-mūrti-śakti-śivābhyāṃ Namaḥ. Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Āṃ Namaḥ. To Śrīkaṇṭha-mūrti-pūrṇo-śakti-śivābhyāṃ Namaḥ on the face-circle. On the right eye: Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Iṃ Namaḥ—to Sūkṣmeśa.

To Mūrti Śalmalī Śakti and Śiva, *namaḥ*. In the left eye: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ īṃ namaḥ*—to Trimūrtīśa Mūrti Lolākṣī Śakti and Śiva, *namaḥ*. (L. 2) In the right ear: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ uṃ namaḥ*—to Arghīśa Mūrti Dīrghakoṇā Śakti and Śiva, *namaḥ*. (L. 3) In the left ear: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ūṃ namaḥ*—to Amareśa Mūrti Vartulā Śakti and Śiva, *namaḥ*.

In the right nostril: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ṛṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Bhūteśamūrti and his Śakti-Śiva, Dīrghamukha. In the left nostril: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ṝṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Atidhīśamūrti and his Śakti-Śiva, Gomukhī.
On the right cheek: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ḷṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Sthāneśamūrti and his Śakti-Śiva, Dīrghajihvā.
On the left cheek: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ḷṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Hareśamūrti, Kumbhodarī, Śakti, and Śiva.

(L. 2) On the upper lip: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ eṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Nandīśamūrti, Ūrdhvamukhīśa, Śakti, and Śiva. (L. 3) On the lower lip: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ aiṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Bhautikeśamūrti, Vikrāntamukhīśa, Śakti, and Śiva.

On the upper teeth: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Sadyojāteśa-mūrti and Jvālāmukhī Śakti-Śivā. On the lower teeth: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ auṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Anugraheśa-mūrti and Ulkāmukhī Śakti-Śivā.
On the tongue: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ aṃ namaḥ*—salutation to Akrūreśa-mūrti and Śrīmukhī Śakti-Śivā.

In the mouth: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ aḥ namaḥ*—salutation to the Mahāseneśa-form, Vyāpinī-Śakti, and Śiva. (L. 2) On the right upper arm: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ kaṃ namaḥ*—salutation to the Asitāṅga-Bhairaveśa-form, Mahākālī-Śakti, and Śiva. (L. 3) On the right wrist: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ khaṃ namaḥ*—salutation to the Krodhīśa-form, Mahākālī-Śakti, and Śiva. (L. 4)

On the right wrist: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ gaṃ namaḥ*—salutation to the form of Caṇḍīśa, to Sarasvatī, and to Śakti and Śiva. (l. 5) On the petal of the right jewel-hand: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ghaṃ namaḥ*—salutation to the form of Pañcāṅgakeśa, to Sarvasiddhi, and to Śakti and Śiva.

On the tip of the right index finger: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ*—salutation to the *Śivottameśa-mūrti* and to the *Trailokyavidyā-śaktiśiva*. (l. 2) On the left upper arm: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ caṃ namaḥ*—salutation to the *Ekarudreśa-mūrti* and to the *Mantravidyā-śaktiśiva*.
On the left elbow: *oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ chaṃ namaḥ*—salutation to the *Kūrmeśa-mūrti* and to the *Ātma-śaktiśiva*. (l. 4)
At the left wrist: Oṃ Śrīṃ. [End of document.]
